sentences.text: Challenge is made to the order dated 17.09.2021 passed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate in rejecting the application filed under Section 77 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that on 31.01.2013, the Food Inspector conducted inspection of a Paan shop of the petitioner and seven retail packs of restricted Rajshree Gutka was found.
They were seized.

On 06.03.2014 a complaint was filed against the petitioner for offence under Section 3(1) (zx), 26(2)(i)(ii)(v) read with Section 51, 52(i) and 59(i) of the Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 and Regulation 2.3.4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restriction on Sales)
Regulation, 2011.

entities.text:
Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restriction on Sales)
Regulation, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The learned Magistrate has taken cognizance on the complaint on 06.03.2014 and issued summons for the presence of the accused.

The accused filed an application under Section 77 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 raising a specific objection that as per Section 77 of the Act of 2006, the Court cannot take cognizance of the offence after one year from the date of commission of offence, therefore, prayed for discharging of the accused.
No 2 MCRC-50185-2021 reply was filed by the respondent.
They have orally opposed the same.

4. The learned Trial Court on 27.07.2017 already framed charges in the matter, therefore, it was observed that the petitioner is already protected and his objection will be considered after recording of evidence.

sentences.text: It is his case that a specific time limit for prosecution is provided in terms of Section 77 of the Act of 2006 wherein it is specifically provided that no Court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act after the expiry of the period of one year from the date of commission of an offence.
It is argued that Section 77 contains non-obstante clause and it specifically bars the Court from taking cognizance and a complaint is made after a period of one year.

It is his case that the inspection of the shop was carried out on 31.03.2013 and complaint was filed on 06.03.2014 that is admittedly after a period of one year from the date of commission of offence.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent has vehemently opposed the application and has supported the order passed by the learned Trial Court for taking cognizance in the matter.
It is argued that under Section 77 of the Act of 2006 a proviso is there which provides for extending period upto three years.
The learned Trial Court has considered the application filed by the petitioner and it was pointed out that cognizance was already taken on 06.03.2014.
No objections were raised at the relevant time.
The complainant evidence has already been recorded in the matter.
The case is listed for recording defence evidence and rejected the application.

It is argued that there is nothing on record to show that cognizance in the matter could not have been taken or whether the Commissioner has granted permission to lodge a prosecution after expiry of one year.
No document pertaining to the same is available on record.
The matter was placed before the concerned authority for taking sanction for 3 MCRC-50185-2021 prosecution and on 16.01.2014, the sanction was granted.
Immediately thereafter the matter was placed before the concerned Court.
There is no illegality.
He has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.
Challenge to the complaint made by the Food Safety Officer is made on the ground that there is non compliance of Section 77 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

The same reads as under :-
"77.

Time limit for prosecution:- Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, no Court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act after the expiry of the period of one year from the date of commission of an offence Provided that the Commissioner of Food Safety may for the reasons to be recorded in writing, approve prosecution within an extended period of upto three years."
9.

There is a proviso being provided which extends the time for filing the complaint upto three years,
in case the Commissioner of Food Safety for the reasons to be recorded in writing, approve the prosecution within an extended period of upto three years.
The record indicates that the inspection was carried out on 31.01.2013.
The sanction for prosecution was granted on 16.01.2014 which is not disputed.
Thereafter the complaint was filed on 06.03.2014 and on the same day the cognizance was taken by the learned Trial Court.
There is no document on record to show that the period for filing a complaint for raising a prosecution was extended by the Commissioner.
On the contrary the sanction for prosecution was given on 16.01.2014 i.e. within a period of one year from the date of inspection.
There is no explanation on record to show that why the complaint was preferred after a period of one year.

There is a specific bar in terms of Section 77 for taking cognizance for offence Poonamchand Joshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141754709/
2 registered in terms of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Punjab Vs. Sarwan Singh reported in AIR 1981 SC 1054 has clearly held that bar of limitation on prosecution was to prevent the parties from filing cases after a long time, as a result of which material evidence may disappear and to prevent the abuse of the process of the Court by filing vexatious and belated prosecutions after a long delay.

entities.text: State of Punjab Vs. Sarwan Singh reported in AIR 1981 SC 1054
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The object of the statute is clear to avoid unwanted litigation.
The same was considered by this Court in M.Cr.C.No.10677 of 2016 (Dayachand Vs. State of M.P.) on 23.01.2017.

entities.text: M.Cr.C.No.10677 of 2016 (Dayachand Vs. State of M.P.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Under these circumstances,
the order taking cognizance in the matter is per se illegal.
The complaint made by the respondent was after a period of one year from the date of carrying out the inspection, despite the fact that the sanction was granted on 16.01.2014 as per the records.
The petitioner cannot be permitted to face unwanted litigation before the Court.
11. Under these circumstances, the order impugned dated 17.09.2021 rejecting the application and order dated 06.03.2014 taking cognizance is hereby quashed.
Consequently the complaint being belated is also quashed.
12. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
